meta.note: Sole price table for the project (report 98 C-07). No build_cost, purchase_cost, upkeep or repair-price column may exist in any other data file.

tax._happiness_coeff_note: 220 -> 360 (Wave-7 ruling, doc 92 sec 20, doc 93 sec E2). happiness_tax_delta(r) = -(r - TAX_RATE_BASE) * this, so at TAX_RATE_MAX the top detent now costs -25.2 happiness points instead of -15.4, and TAX_RATE_ATTRACT_PULL turns the same points into an attractiveness ceiling of 0.6724 instead of 0.7998. ONE key moves BOTH couplings because both are denominated in these points - the rate is read exactly once in the whole chain (see _attract_pull_note). WHY: Wave 6 made the grid buyable, which gave tax_squeezer somewhere to spend 1.778x revenue, and on the 21-game-day matrix it ended AHEAD of balanced on population (+43%) as well as on value (+104%) for a happiness deficit of 1.6 points - strictly dominant again. Fitted on gate 12b's controlled pair and confirmed on the 3-seed matrix: 340 leaves the squeezer only 5.5% behind on population (misses the ruled 10%), 400 takes it BELOW balanced on cash (a trap, not a tradeoff), 360 lands -14.7% population / 23.0 happiness points / +35% value created. NOTHING at or below TAX_RATE_BASE moves - the delta is exactly 0 at 0.09 - so every founding anchor and every state hash is bit-identical (verified with tools/profile_sim.gd --baseline on both the starter city and tests/fixtures/bench_city.json). TAX_RATE_GROWTH_COEFF, TAX_RATE_ATTRACT_PULL, TAX_RATE_MIN/MAX and every revenue term are untouched.
tax._growth_coeff_note: 3.5 -> 8.0 (doc 92 pass-2 F-5 ruling). At 3.5 the top detent bought +46% value created for an 11% population cost and was strictly dominant; at 8.0 the top detent multiplies growth by 0.44 and the bottom by 1.40, so the slider is money-now versus a-city-later. Revenue is untouched: TAX_RATE_HAPPINESS_COEFF, TAX_RATE_MIN/MAX and the policy factor all hold.
tax._attract_pull_note: NEW, doc 09 amendment T-1 (the tax-growth coupling). TAX_RATE_GROWTH_COEFF alone CANNOT bite a healthy city: it scales the RATE at which doc 09's A_city relaxes toward attractiveness_target(stability), and that target saturates at 1.00 for any stability >= 0.85, so a founding city sits at target and the multiplier scales zero (doc 92 pass-2, gate 12). This key is the missing half - it prices the tax slider into the TARGET. attractiveness_tax_factor(r) = 1 + 1.30 * min(0, happiness_tax_delta(r)) / 100, i.e. the rate is converted to happiness points ONCE (by TAX_RATE_HAPPINESS_COEFF) and spent on doc 09's attractiveness scale, never read twice. At the top detent the delta is -25.2 points (Wave-7 coefficient 360), the factor is 0.6724, and the ceiling is 0.6724: one resident in three leaves. At and below TAX_RATE_BASE the factor is 1.0 - the bottom detent buys a 1.40x faster refill through TAX_RATE_GROWTH_COEFF, not a higher ceiling. Doc 09 owns the mapping and composes the three ceilings with min(), so the same discontent is never billed twice; its happiness-side coefficient PopulationSystem.ATTRACT_HAPPINESS_PULL is authored to this same 1.30 because both act on happiness points.
tax._tax_level_note: The player knob of doc 03 §2.2 is the RATE r, bounded by TAX_RATE_MIN/MAX. cmd_set_tax_level exposes it as the discrete ladder MIN, MIN+STEP, ... , MAX so the UI has detents; level 5 lands exactly on TAX_RATE_BASE. The ladder is computed in basis points so no float drift can move a detent off its authored rate. Note this is the tax RATE ladder and has nothing to do with TAX_LEVEL_GROWTH, which is base_tax growth per BUILDING level.
tax._stability_note: S is [0,1] from doc 09 (C-56). f_stability = STAB_FLOOR + (1-STAB_FLOOR) * S^STAB_EXP. No /100.
tax._cond_floor_note: COND_FLOOR 0.55 -> 0.40 (doc 92 sec 13.3, Wave-4 ruling 2). f_condition = COND_FLOOR + (1 - COND_FLOOR) * C, so the floor sets THE PAYBACK PERIOD OF A REPAIR: payback_gh = capital x REPAIR_COST_PER_CAPITAL / (base_tax x (1 - COND_FLOOR)), with the damage fraction cancelling. A house L1 pays back in 453 gh (18.9 game-days) at 0.55 and 340 gh (14.2) at 0.40 -- 18.9 is OUTSIDE doc 03 sec 2.12's pacing horizon, which is the mechanical reason doc 92 pass-2 F-2 measured the agent that never repairs beating the one that does. Measured A/B at 21 game-days, seed 1337: balanced/neglect treasury $37,808/$65,668 at 0.55 and $65,845/$59,971 at 0.40. f_condition(1.0) = 1.0 at every floor, so no founding anchor moves; doc 03 sec 2.2's worked examples A/B re-price to 0.9700 / $23.68 / $8.17 and tests/test_economy.gd carries them.
tax._tax_yield_note: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY (RR-5). The published base_tax_by_level rows in data/buildings.json and the $686/gh starter anchor are normative; this map documents why the L1 rows have the shape they do and is checked by test 7 as a +/-6% drift guard, never as an equality. Max drift today is 4.76% (store, office).
tax._road_note: f_road consumes doc 10's access_quality(pos) in [0,1] (C-61). This doc defines no road_access_factor.

upgrades._upg_coeff_note: 1.45 -> 1.15 (Wave 17, doc 93 sec Y7, doc 92 sec 43.3). NOT a fit: UPG_COEFF = TAX_LEVEL_GROWTH - 1 is an IDENTITY. Doc 03 sec 2.3's ladders make payback(upgrade L->L+1) = (build_cost_l1/base_tax_l1) x [UPG_COEFF/(TAX_LEVEL_GROWTH-1)] x (UPG_GROWTH/TAX_LEVEL_GROWTH)^(L-1), and build_cost_l1/base_tax_l1 is exactly 100 gh for every revenue archetype, so at UPG_COEFF = TAX_LEVEL_GROWTH - 1 the FIRST rung pays back in exactly the time a fresh building does and the ruled window [100, 200] gh holds for all five rungs (measured 98.6 / 121.3 / 140.2 / 167.0 / 197.8). At 1.45 the ladder was 124.3 / 153.0 / 176.8 / 210.6 / 249.4 -- the first rung 24% worse than simply building another house, which is what level 2's `upgrade instead of building more` card taught against (PA-46). PA-46's own proposed ceiling 1.15 x (TAX_LEVEL_GROWTH - 1) = 1.3225 is 15% loose and is superseded: it yields a first rung 15% WORSE than a new build, the opposite of its stated target. CAPITAL_VALUE_V below is re-derived from this coefficient and every cell is now its own closed form at 3 dp.
upgrades._demand_growth_note: RR-7: the requirement is an EXCLUSIVE FLOOR, not an equality. Every doc-02 growth class must satisfy k_dem > REQUIRED_MIN_DEMAND_LEVEL_GROWTH. Doc 02 is the authority on the values (2.35 steady / 2.45 standard / 2.55 vertical, C-13). The old REQUIRED_DEMAND_LEVEL_GROWTH: 2.35 equality constant is DELETED - it rejected 9 of 12 archetypes.
upgrades._v6_note: The sixth cell is NEW (doc 92 §24.4, the level-6 tower tier). It is the only cell of this vector this project ever placed itself and it is placed by the rule the other five claim: the closed form V(6) = 1 + (1.45/1.55)(2.55^5 − 1) = 100.9287528125 exactly, half-up at 3 dp = 100.929. Six of doc 02's twelve archetypes have a level 6; the other six never index past 5 and cannot see this cell.

roads._note: Sole road price table (report 98 RR-2, extending C-07). data/roads.json carries build_cost, upgrade_cost, upkeep_per_game_day and repair_cost_base in NO form. Doc 10 owns road work and physics - crew-hours, condition on [0,1] (RR-3), decay rates, damage fractions - and no prices.
roads._no_upkeep_note: ROADS CARRY NO STANDING PER-TILE UPKEEP IN MVP, mirroring C-08. The recurring cost of a road is decay bought back through the C-16 repair formula; see 2.12(f) for the derived starter expectation of $185.87/gh over the 783-tile core, evaluated at doc 10's published starter operating point c_day = 0.35 (RR-13). The $147.22/gh figure Round 2 booked is the c_day = 0 FLOOR, which the sim never observes.
roads._repair_basis_note: capital_value(road tile) = build_cost_per_tile * ROAD_REPAIR_CAPITAL_FRACTION -> STREET 360, AVENUE 1040. Repair re-buys the wearing course and the top of the base, not the excavation, sub-base, utility corridor or right-of-way. A 1.00 basis prices the starter core's routine maintenance at $929.35/gh at c_day 0.35 = 110.7% of gross revenue ($736.12 even at the c_day 0 floor); see 2.5 and 2.12(f).
roads._demolish_note: Same DEMOLITION_REFUND_FRACTION as buildings: STREET $450, AVENUE $1300 per tile.

water._note: Sole water-asset price table (C-07, extended to doc 05's placement verbs the way RR-2 extended it to doc 10's). data/water.json carries no dollar in any form - only the dimensionless price_inputs ratios this block multiplies. Doc 05 owns capacity, kW, condition and work content; doc 03 owns every dollar.
water._component_derivation: No new ladder: a water component is priced off 2.13(a)'s build_cost_l1.water_plant = 45,000, which IS the L1 pump reference variant, through 2.3's own two curves. build(variant, L) = round(45000 * CAPITAL_VALUE_V[L] * price_inputs.variant_cost_ratio_l1[variant]) and upgrade(variant, L -> L+1) = round(upgrade_cost(water_plant, L) * the same ratio). L1: source_river 37,800 / treatment 120,150 / pump 45,000 / tank 59,850.
water._main_derivation: A water main is a BURIED utility run, and 2.13(b) already prices exactly one of those: feeder class 1 at $110/tile overhead x UNDERGROUND_COST_MULT 2.6 = $286/tile. service is anchored there; trunk and arterial follow data/water.json price_inputs.main_cost_ratio_per_tile (2.81 / 7.5), which is what that ratio table exists for. Two independent cross-checks land on it: a 16-tile service segment (M_TIE's length in doc 09 2.9.6) is $4,576 of capital, so C-16 prices a total break at 4,576 x 1.00 x 0.85 = $3,890 against doc 05's DELETED main_break base_cost of $4,000; and a pump's capital is then 45,000 / 4,576 = 9.8x a service segment's, against doc 05 2.12's 'a pump's capital is ~11x a service main segment's'.
water._repair_basis_note: Unlike a road tile (0.20 - repair re-buys the wearing course, not the excavation), a broken main is dug up and replaced in full, so its repair capital IS its build price. capital_value(main) = tiles * main_build_cost_per_tile[tier].
water._demolish_note: The same DEMOLITION_REFUND_FRACTION buildings, grid components and road tiles use.

expenses._maint_condition_penalty_note: HELD at 1.5, measured (doc 92 sec 13.4). building_maint is the single largest expense line in a grown city ($466.89/gh of $1,289.80 at 320 buildings), but isolated on the maintenance-pays A/B a move to 2.5 contributes only +$703 of a $5,874 gap (12%) while charging BOTH agents 8-16% more. COND_FLOOR alone flips the gate. Recorded so it is not re-litigated. WAVE 17: retiring this line outright was tried and WITHDRAWN (doc 93 sec Y1, doc 92 sec 43.8). It bills exactly the four REVENUE_CLASSES -- exactly the buildings the city does not own -- so it reads like the city paying a landlord's repair bill, and the first draft of the ownership ruling retired it on that reading. Measured, that was wrong twice over: the line is the city's cost of SERVING a building (which is what C-08's civic exclusion implies, since civic shells are excluded because their own O&M lines bill them), and with it gone AND private stock kept up by its owners, tools/measure_insolvency.gd put do_nothing on `standard` at game-day 176 against gate 29's ruled 69 while `casual` never went insolvent inside 200 game-days at all. What the 2026-09-01 playtest asked to move to the owner is the lumpy TAPPED repair, and E_OWNER_MAINTAINED is what moves it.
expenses._repair_note: repair_cost = capital_value * damage_fraction * REPAIR_COST_PER_CAPITAL * M_repair (C-16). Docs 02/04/05/06/07 supply damage_fraction only and hold no price table.
expenses._rush_derivation: NEW, doc 03 sec 2.13(f) / report 98 RR-107 (Wave 17, the rush verb). NOT AN INVENTED NUMBER: it is the two cells above, re-expressed. The emergency-contractor row buys (1 - CONTRACTOR_TIME_FRACTION) = 0.65 of a project's duration for a surcharge of (CONTRACTOR_SURCHARGE - 1) = 0.80 of its cash price, so this doc's published price of time is 0.80 / 0.65 = 1.230769... of the cash price per unit of FULL duration. cmd_rush_construction buys the remaining (1 - progress) of a project's duration and pays exactly that rate, so a rush at zero progress costs 1.23077x the cash price and the two valves are the same value per hour saved by construction - neither dominates, and doc 03 sec 2.5's 'deliberately bad value' verdict is inherited rather than re-argued. CostCurves re-checks this cell against the contractor pair at load (RUSH_DERIVATION_TOLERANCE 1e-5) so it cannot drift away from its own derivation.
expenses._station_staffing_note: RR-16: where E_grid or E_water already bills a facility's O&M, that service's department line is STAFFING ONLY and says so here. water_works 20 is staffing only - the water works' plant O&M is E_water's pump_capacity_m3h * PUMP_OM_PER_M3H_HOUR ($14.00/gh on the starter pump). Power plants and substations carry NO station_upkeep row at all: E_grid's PLANT_OM_PER_MW_HOUR and GRID_MAINT_PER_MW_HOUR bill them in full (C-08 no-double-billing). No value changed under RR-16.
expenses._vehicle_note: Sole vehicle price table (C-07 / R-14). purchase for the five doc-06 MVP types = round_to_100(9000 * (purchase_06/45000)^0.32631), anchored so fire_engine = 1.60 x patrol_car. dispatch_cost = round(2.4 * upkeep). upkeep and active_mult are authored per role.
expenses._grid_cost_note: Rescaled from doc 04 onto this ladder (C-07). Doc 04's build_cost, upkeep_per_gh and fuel_cost_per_kwh columns are deleted; recurring grid cost is E_grid above, generation fuel is FUEL_PRICE_PER_MWH.

_tariffs_note: POLICE_FINE_PER_RESOLVED_INCIDENT 350 is DELETED here (report 98 RR-78). It was the same dollar as doc 06's reward_base[crime] 350 and only one of the two was ever live; the survivor is city_services.dispatch_payout_base below. Doc 06 open question 6 asked for this ruling in Wave 1 and doc 93 sec N1 point 4 wrote its re-open condition; both are discharged.

storm_prep._source: 07-weather-disaster-director.md §2.7.7's six preparation actions, priced HERE because doc 03 owns every dollar (C-07). data/director.json's storm.prep_actions keeps only the dimensionless knobs doc 07 owns - travel_time_mult, fill_to, progress_loss_min, drain_rate_mult, duration_min, power_load_mult - and carries no dollar in any form. Read through CostCurves.storm_prep_cost().
storm_prep._derivation: pre_stage_crews_per_crew 3,000 / callout_crew 18,000 / sandbag_block 6,000 are doc 07 §2.7.7's own authored figures, moved and not edited (the same move data/incidents.json's reward_base made under RR-78). top_off_water_per_m3 is the one that had to be derived, because §2.7.7 says only '$ per m³ (doc 05)': a tank L1 costs $59,850 for 120 m³ of capacity (§2.13(b)'s water ladder, data/water.json's own capacity column), which is $498.75 per m³ of STORAGE; an emergency fill buys the water and not the tank, and 1 % of the stored capital per m³ is $4.99 -> 5. A half-empty L1 tank tops off for $300 and a city on L4 tanks pays about $4,400 a tank, which sits between the sandbag and the crew callout - the intended shape, since topping off is the cheap insurance and the callout is the expensive one.

city_services._note: NEW, report 98 RR-78 (the money pass). Sole payout table for doc 06's dispatch and doc 12's street opportunities - the last dollar column that lived outside this file. data/incidents.json carried reward_base and no longer does; data/street.json still carries the LIVE reward columns this table is due to absorb (single-source migration is the next balance touch, with the 57%-ceiling retune). The split of ownership is the same one C-16 uses for repairs: doc 06 owns the SHAPE of a payout - which tier it peaked at, how fast the city answered, whether a human made the call - and doc 03 owns every dollar in it.
city_services._double_booking_ruling: RR-78 answers doc 06 open question 6, held since Wave 1. reward_base[crime] 350 and POLICE_FINE_PER_RESOLVED_INCIDENT 350 ARE the same dollar. Only doc 06's was live - credited straight to the treasury on resolve, in no ledger line and no notification - while doc 03's was a HELD metering constant (CitySim.HELD_FINE_RATE = 3/350, measured flat at $3.00/gh on every preset at the founding hour, at 21 game-days and at 48, doc 93 sec N1 point 3). Doc 93 sec N1 point 4 wrote the re-open condition down: 'when doc 06 publishes real resolutions, the line becomes a measurement'. It has. The held pair and the `fines` ledger line are retired; the live `city_services` line below replaces them.
city_services._base_note: MOVED, NOT RETUNED - these are doc 06 sec 2.7's reward_base column to the dollar. Auto-dispatch therefore keeps exactly the dollars it has quietly earned since Wave 1, which is what lets the do_nothing and infrastructure_first control columns of the balance matrix move ONLY through the grants block below. The new money this wave pays out is the dispatcher's premium, and a control agent never earns one.
city_services._manual_mult_note: 1.50 is doc 06 sec 2.7's own speed_bonus_max, adopted rather than invented: the game already prices a perfect response at 1.50x and a human on the incident drawer is worth exactly that. It applies only when Incident.manual_requested is true - i.e. only through cmd_dispatch_unit - so an auto-dispatched incident pays 1.00x and the premium is 50%, visible in one glance at the budget panel. The player's ask was two-sided ('our automatic dispatch in crime, that should pay us money' AND a reason to work the drawer); auto keeps its money and the ledger finally names it, and the drawer is where the raise is.
city_services._cap_derivation: The guard: a payout may never exceed the loss it prevented, or letting a fire grow becomes a strategy. prevented_loss(inc) = capital_value(target) - repair_cost(target, residual_damage_fraction) - what you kept, net of what you spent keeping it. Three constraints place 0.75. (1) FLOOR: doc 06 sec 2.7's ruled worked example - tier-3 fire, house L2, on scene at minute 5 - pays $1,657 against a prevented loss of $2,940 - $500 = $2,440, i.e. 0.679, and a cap below that would retune a ruled payout at its own reference point. (2) CEILING: at 1.00 the player is indifferent between a fire and no fire, and indifference plus variance is a strategy, so the cap is strictly below it. (3) 0.75 is the midpoint of [0.679, 1.00) to the nearest 0.05. THE GUARD BINDS ON SHIPPED NUMBERS AND THAT IS THE FINDING: the same house at tier 5 resolved at target speed pays 900 * 2.40 * 1.00 = $2,160 against a prevented loss of 2,940 - 1,000 = $1,940 (ratio 1.11), and at best speed $3,240 (ratio 1.67). Doc 06's reward curve grows with tier_k 0.35 while doc 02's residual-damage curve grows at 0.10/tier, so on a cheap building the reward outruns the value at risk from tier 4 up. See doc 92 sec 35.3.
city_services._unpriced_ceiling_derivation: The absolute dollar ceiling for the three types whose targets doc 03 prices no capital for - traffic_accident and storm_damage/blocked_road (a road edge) and water_main_break (a water segment). Derived from the most expensive single asset a road-class response protects: doc 03 sec 2.13(d) rebuilds a COLLAPSED AVENUE tile at the full build price, $5,200, and MORAL_HAZARD_CAP_FRACTION 0.75 x 5,200 = $3,900. It is deliberately the LOOSE bound and says so - a tight one needs doc 05 to price a water segment and doc 10 to price a closed-segment hour, and neither exists - but it has teeth where it matters: the worst case any of the three can pay today is tier 5 at the best speed with a human on the drawer, i.e. base x 2.40 x 1.50 x 1.50 = base x 5.40, so traffic_accident pays at most $1,620, storm_damage $2,160 and water_main_break $2,700, and raising water_main_break's base past 722 would fail gate 31. THE FARMING VECTOR IS NOT HERE, which is why a loose bound is honest: a moral hazard needs an asset the player owns and could choose to let burn, and those are exactly the priced targets the runtime clamp covers.
city_services._cap_scope_note: The runtime clamp binds only where doc 03 can price the asset: buildings (capital_value by archetype and level) and grid components (capital_value_grid). Road edges and water segments have no capital_value in this file, so prevented_loss returns -1 there and the clamp is SKIPPED rather than silently zeroing a payout - the published table is what holds those types, and tests/test_balance_gates.gd gate 31 is what holds the published table.
city_services._street_payout_migration: LIVE SINCE 2026-08-21 (report 98 RR-85, doc 92 §39.1). Until this pass these were three PLACEHOLDER flats that nothing read: `data/street.json` carried the live `reward: {base, spread}` columns and `OpportunitySystem` priced every bounty out of them, so doc 03 published one set of dollars and the game paid another. The live columns are now HERE, to the dollar and to the spread, and street.json refuses them back (`OpportunitySystem.FORBIDDEN_KEYS`) exactly as data/incidents.json refuses `reward_base`. The migration MOVED NO NUMBER — every determinism baseline is bit-identical across it, which is the check that it was a move and not a retune.
city_services._street_payout_shape: reward = round((base + spread*u) * (1 + STREET_REWARD_CITY_LEVEL_K * (city_level - 1))), u ~ U[0,1) drawn once on the `street` stream at SPAWN and frozen onto the row, so the map marker, the preview, the commit and a save->load all quote the same dollars. `base` is the floor of the kind's band and `base + spread` its top; the MEAN bounty of a kind is `base + spread/2` and that is the figure every ruling below is stated against, because a band's mean is what a player earns and its top is what a player remembers.
city_services._street_note: data/street.json owns WHEN an opportunity appears, WHERE it stands, how long it lives and what it looks like; it owns no dollar. The three kinds sit under doc 06's dispatch payouts by ruling — a tapped crook is petty, a dispatched crime is the real one — and `_street_petty_ratio_ruling` is where that ratio is finally stated against a number the game actually pays.
city_services._street_petty_ratio_ruling: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-21 (doc 92 §39.3), and the DERIVATION moved while the ruling did not. The ruling has always been 'a tapped crook is petty, a dispatched crime is the real one, and the ratio has to read as about half at a glance'; the placeholder stated it as 180/350 = 0.514 against `dispatch_payout_base.crime`. THAT DENOMINATOR IS NOT A PAYOUT. 350 is a BASE that doc 06 multiplies by tier (1 + 0.35*(tier_peak-1)) and by a speed bonus on [0.60, 1.50] before anybody is paid; the crime a player actually watches resolve is doc 06's own reference case — tier 3, answered on target — which pays 350 * 1.70 * 1.00 = $595 (doc 92 §38.1's table, row `crime`). Against THAT, the live street bounty's mean of 260 + 90/2 = $305 is 0.513 — the ruled 'about half' to three decimal places, and within 0.002 of the ratio the placeholder claimed. So the live table already honours the ruling and NOTHING RETUNES; what was wrong was the number the gate compared against, and gate 32(b) now compares against the reference payout instead of the base.
city_services._street_rate_contract: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-21 (doc 92 §39.4). This is the ruled ceiling on the spawn table's UN-REJECTED offer rate, `1 / data/street.json spawn.target_interval_h`, and it is a contract gate 32 can finally CHECK: before RR-85 the spawn table lived in a sibling branch's file, so the old 0.45 was multiplied by a placeholder payout and compared against nothing that constrained it — and the shipped table has run at 0.667/gh since the layer landed, i.e. the old bound was violated by 48% from the day it was written and no test could see it. The ceiling is 0.70 because the shipped table sits at 0.6667 and doc 06 §2.16's own beat band is 1-3 real minutes between offers: delivery is always at or below the un-rejected rate (max_live, min_separation_tiles and an empty kerb pool take their share, and the measured delivery is 0.567/gh = 1.76 real minutes), so a table above 0.70 would be crowding the band's fast edge before rejections and is refused. IT IS A TRIPWIRE, NOT A FIT: it refuses any target_interval_h under 1.43. THE DOLLAR BOUND IS NO LONGER DERIVED FROM IT — see STREET_CEILING_SHARE_MAX, which is measured.
city_services._street_ceiling_derivation: NEW 2026-08-21 (doc 92 §39.2), and it replaces a worst-case product with a measurement. THE CEILING is what the layer pays a player who collects EVERY offer — not what a session earns, and doc 92 §35.3's ruling is stated on it: 'the ceiling belongs nearer 35-40 %', high enough to answer 'make money quickly', low enough that tapping never outruns running a city. §35.3 measured 57% and asked for a retune. IT RE-MEASURES AT 35.9% AND NOTHING RETUNES, because the retune already happened on the other side of the ratio: the money pass (RR-78/RR-79) raised the founding net anchor 337.05 -> 506.05/gh, and the same $181.65/gh ceiling that was 57% of the old net is 35.90% of the one the opening actually earns. The share was fixed by making the city richer rather than by making the street poorer, which is the outcome §35.3 said it preferred ('the crook and the dog are the kinds carrying the fiction the player asked for'). 0.40 is the top of §35.3's own band and leaves 4.1 points of headroom; gate 32(d) measures the ceiling on the real spawner and holds it there.
city_services._street_played_band_derivation: NEW 2026-08-21 (doc 92 §39.5). The band the OLD `_street_rate_contract` claimed - 'the ruled band is 10-20% of early-game income WHEN PLAYED' - was never measured, because until this pass no agent in tools/playtest.gd could tap. `collector` can (RR-86), and the number is now taken on a 21-game-day arc rather than derived from a rate constant: street income as a share of the same run's net. The floor is 0.05 and not 0.10 because the ARC is not the opening - the collector's street income grows with STREET_REWARD_CITY_LEVEL_K (1.8x by level 5) while a curriculum city's net grows about 3x, so the share DECAYS across the run by construction, and a floor fitted to the founding hour would fail on a city that simply got rich. The ceiling stays 0.20: a layer that pays a fifth of a played city's income is a strong second income and anything above it is the inversion gate 32 exists to refuse.
city_services._street_level_k_note: MOVED from data/street.json `spawn.reward_city_level_k` on 2026-08-21 (RR-85), value unchanged. It is a term in a DOLLAR formula, so it is doc 03's under C-07 - the spawn table may say how often a crook appears and may not say what he is worth. A level-5 city pays 1.8x a founding one, so the layer stays worth crossing the map for after the treasury has grown. MEASURED at last on an arc (doc 92 §39.6, closing §35.3's second-order question 4, which the founding-city ceiling could not ask because it never left level 0): over 3 seeds x 21 game-days the `collector` agent's mean bounty tracks this multiplier to within 2.9% at every level from 2 to 5 - 1.221/1.371/1.554/1.840 measured against 1.200/1.400/1.600/1.800 authored - so the formula does what it says. And the city OUTRUNS it: 1.84x the founding bounty at level 5 against a run net of $1,669/gh on a founding $506.05/gh, i.e. 3.30x, about 1.8 to one. That is the direction that keeps the street a second income and not a first one, and it is why 0.20 is HELD rather than raised.
city_services._street_idle_note: Not a knob - a written-down zero. An uncollected opportunity pays nothing, expires, and books no revenue anywhere; the line is 0 for a player who never taps one. This key exists so that 'and 0 when idle' is a thing a test can read rather than a thing a doc claims.

grants._note: NEW, report 98 RR-79 (the early-income retune). Two grants, one hourly and one lumpy, both authored here because both are dollars (C-07). Neither is farmable: the hourly one is a published constant on a clock that runs out, and the lumpy one pays once per city level for the life of a city.
grants._founding_assistance_derivation: 172 is not a fit - it is doc 03 sec 2.12's own founding `departments` ($96.00/gh) plus `fleet` ($76.00/gh), the two operating lines the player is billed for and never chose. A founded city is handed three stations and eight vehicles by data/starter_city.json and starts paying full price for them in game-hour 1; that is the mechanical reason the opening reads slow, and it is measurable: those two lines are $172.00 of a $504.73/gh expense bill against $841.22 of gross, i.e. 34.1% of everything the city spends before it has built anything. The state covers them at founding and hands them back on a straight line over FOUNDING_ASSISTANCE_DAYS: share(day) = clamp(1 - day / 7, 0, 1), evaluated on the settled game-day so the line steps once a day rather than drifting inside one. It is a published constant and NOT a fraction of the live bill, deliberately - a subsidy that grew with the fleet would pay a player to buy vehicles, and a revenue line carrying an M_exp inside it would break doc 03 test 46's one-knob-per-line contract (doc 93 sec N1).
grants._founding_assistance_window: 7 game-days is the curriculum's own opening: doc 92 sec 27.4 measures curriculum level 3 arriving at game-hour 122-128, i.e. game-day 5.1-5.3, so the taper covers levels 1-3 with a day and a half of margin and is fully retired before level 4's incident wait begins. Total paid over the window is 172 * 24 * (7+6+5+4+3+2+1)/7 = 172 * 24 * 4 = $16,512, against a founding purse of $25,000. Note the DISCRETE daily step, not the continuous integral: the share is evaluated once per settled game-day, so the seven daily shares average 4/7 = 0.5714 rather than 0.5, and a reader who integrates gets $14,448 and is $2,064 light.
grants._level_up_grant_derivation: Indexed by city level; index 0 is the founding level and pays nothing. The rule is one sentence - THE CITY PAYS HALF OF WHAT THE NEXT CHAPTER ASKS YOU TO BUY - applied to doc 09 sec 2.14's curriculum row above each rung and rounded to a readable figure: level 1 celebrates and level 2 teaches two stores at $2,600 each plus an upgrade (half of ~$5,200 -> 2,500); level 2 -> level 3's apartment $7,000 + four street tiles $7,200 = $14,200 (-> 7,000); level 3 -> level 4's police station $18,000 (-> 9,000); level 4 -> level 5's water works $45,000 (-> 22,500); level 5 -> level 6's $73,572 tower upgrade (-> 37,000). Level 6 is the top rung and has no chapter above it, so its grant is the extrapolation the rung itself is (doc 92 sec 24.6, thresholds note): 37,000 * 2.25 = 83,250, published as 83,000. Labelled honest extrapolation, exactly as rungs 4 and 5 of the population ladder are.
grants._level_up_grant_scope: Paid by ProgressionSystem on the level TRANSITION, once per level per city, on whichever route earned it - the population ladder or doc 09's objectives (doc 93 sec G1 composes them with max(), and this pays the composed level so neither route is worth more than the other). A one-off receipt is NOT an hourly ledger line, for the same reason doc 03 sec 2.4 keeps one-off capital spends out of the recurring rate: it is a treasury event and a notification, and the budget panel's income statement stays an income statement.

building_repair._comment: 99-PA PA-33 / report 98 RR-150 (Wave 18). The player's say over doc 02 §2.6's building repair, mirroring doc 10 §2.13's road pair. TWO dials and NOT ONE PRICE: doc 03 owns every dollar (C-07) and this block authors none of them — `cmd_repair_building(sim_id, true)` is asked for every quote, exactly the same call the panel's REPAIR button makes, so the policy and the button can never disagree about what a repair costs. The CAP is a player BUDGET, not a price: it is how much of its own money the city is willing to spend on repairs in a game-day, which is the same thing `data/roads.json`'s auto_repair_default_daily_cap is and is why it lives with the money rather than with doc 02's physics.
building_repair._bands_note: The threshold ladder names doc 02 §2.6's OWN band keys and copies no number: `CitySim` resolves `band_worn` / `band_good` through the building's stamped `condition` rules (Building.rule, PA-13's accessor), so a policy rung and the band a player is told about are the same value by construction, and re-authoring building_rules.json moves both. `off` is 0.0 and is the SHIPPED DEFAULT — RR-150: a default that spent the treasury without being asked would move every gate in the balance matrix in a wave whose job is to surface what the money already does, so a city that never opens the control is bit-identical to the Wave-17 fork.
building_repair._cap_derivation: 10000 is one game-day of the measured civic repair bill with headroom, not a round number: tools/measure_repair_burden.gd --days=45 --seeds=1337 --strategies=curriculum measures $226,852 of civic repair across 45 game-days = $5,041/game-day averaged, peaking at $55,249 in the 36-42 bucket (7 days = $7,893/day). A $10,000/day cap therefore pays the whole bill on an ordinary day and throttles a catch-up spike into two or three days instead of emptying the treasury in one, which is what a budget is for. The ladder's rungs are the same shape data/roads.json uses: off, a cautious rung, the default, and two rungs for a city that would rather spend than tap.
